topic: Template Metaprogramming with Expression Templates and Compile-Time Evaluation
explanation: Expression templates are a powerful C++ metaprogramming technique that allows for the compile-time evaluation of expressions, significantly improving performance, particularly in numerical computation.  They avoid the creation of temporary objects during expression evaluation by representing expressions as abstract syntax trees (ASTs) at compile time.  The compiler then optimizes the expression directly into efficient machine code, often eliminating unnecessary intermediate results and memory allocations. This contrasts sharply with traditional operator overloading, which typically involves the creation of temporary objects for each operation.  The implementation relies heavily on template specialization and recursion to build and evaluate the AST at compile time.
keywords: Expression Templates, Template Metaprogramming, Compile-Time Evaluation, zero-overhead abstraction
